title: Evaluation of Pollen Grains and Fertility in Citrus
author: Shingo Goto
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.q78dzrw
materials: The anthers were removed from each flower with forceps, and then immersed into 50 μl of lactophenol blue solution (Merck Millipore, Billerica, MA, USA) with shaking at 300 rpm for 1 h at room temperature. 10–15 anthers were used in an individual flower which has less than 500 of pollen grains per anther, and 3–5 anthers were used in that has more than 500 of pollen grains per anther.

steps.title: Collect and store flowers
steps.instruction: Collect three representative citrus flowers per seedling immediately after full bloom during anthesis, place them in plastic containers with silica gel, and store at –30 °C until evaluation.

steps.title: Dehisce anthers and shake
steps.instruction: Using forceps, dehisce the anthers, then place them on a shaker and agitate at the same speed for an additional two hours.

steps.title: Prepare pollen suspension and image
steps.instruction: Disperse the released pollen grains in lactophenol blue solution, transfer an aliquot onto a Thoma hemocytometer (0.1 mm depth, Nitirin, Tokyo, Japan), and capture four photographs per flower under a Nikon Eclipse 80iR microscope equipped with a digital camera; if fewer than 10 pollen grains appear per microscope field, capture ten photographs instead.

steps.title: Count pollen grains with ImageJ
steps.instruction: Open the digital images in ImageJ (http://imagej.nih.gov/ij/) using the ‘cell counter’ plug‑in, count the pollen grains in each image, compute the average number of grains from the 4 or 10 photographs, and determine the number of pollen grains per anther based on three flowers per seedling.

steps.title: Calculate apparent pollen fertility
steps.instruction: Determine the ratio of densely stained pollen grains to the total pollen grains (stained + unstained) as apparent fertility; count 30–50 grains in a flower whose anther contains <500 grains, or 50–200 grains if the anther contains >500 grains, and calculate the ratio using data from three flowers per seedling.
